## Overview

Landmark configurations in two or three dimensions are stored as a real
`k × m × n` array: `k` landmarks, `m = 2` or `3` coordinates, `n`
configurations. The functions below work on such arrays directly. The
complex 2D interface described in the getting-started vignette is
unchanged.

## Simulating 3D shapes

`sim_shapes3d()` draws two groups of configurations around a cube and a
parallelepiped template with Gaussian landmark noise, after a random
rotation of each configuration. Here `n` is the number of configurations
per group.

```{r simulate}
library(ShapeClust)

sim <- sim_shapes3d(n = 20, sigma = 0.5, seed = 1)
dim(sim$X)
table(sim$group)
```

## Distances

`shape_distance()` returns the Riemannian (`"rho"`), full Procrustes
(`"dF"`) or partial Procrustes (`"dP"`) distance matrix. Reflections are
kept as distinct shapes unless `reflection = TRUE`.

```{r distance}
D <- shape_distance(sim$X, "rho")
dim(D)
round(range(D[upper.tri(D)]), 3)
```

## Clustering

`shape_kmeans()` runs Lloyd's algorithm with a Procrustes mean shape.
`shape_pam()` and `shape_rankkmed()` accept the array as well (they
compute `shape_distance()` internally) or a distance matrix.

```{r clustering}
set.seed(1)
fit_km  <- shape_kmeans(sim$X, K = 2)
fit_pam <- shape_pam(sim$X, K = 2)

table(group = sim$group, kmeans = fit_km$cluster)
table(group = sim$group, pam = fit_pam$cluster)
cat("FMI, k-means:", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_km$cluster), 3), "\n")
cat("FMI, PAM    :", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_pam$cluster), 3), "\n")
```

## Bagging

`bagclust1()` takes the same array. With `base = "kmeans"`, each
bootstrap replicate fits the centers on the resample and labels all `n`
configurations by the nearest center; the medoid-based bases (`"pam"`,
`"rankkmed"`, `"clarans"`, `"hill"`) work on the distance matrix.

```{r bagging}
fit_bag <- bagclust1(sim$X, K = 2, base = "pam", B = 30, seed = 1)
table(group = sim$group, bagged = fit_bag$cluster)
cat("FMI, bagged PAM:", round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_bag$cluster), 3), "\n")

fit_bagk <- bagclust1(sim$X, K = 2, base = "kmeans", B = 10, seed = 1)
cat("FMI, bagged k-means:",
    round(fmi_index(sim$group, fit_bagk$cluster), 3), "\n")
```

## Clustering tendency

`hopkins_shape()` tests whether a sample has cluster structure, with a
Monte Carlo p-value under a tangent-space Gaussian null.

```{r hopkins}
hopkins_shape(sim$X, B = 49, seed = 1)
```

## A real data example: macaque skulls

The `macaques` data of the **shapes** package are 7 landmarks in 3D on 18
skulls, nine female and nine male.

```{r macaques, eval = requireNamespace("shapes", quietly = TRUE)}
data(macaques, package = "shapes")
X <- macaques$x
sex <- macaques$group
dim(X)
table(sex)

set.seed(1)
fit_pam <- shape_pam(X, K = 2)
fit_bag <- bagclust1(X, K = 2, base = "pam", B = 50, seed = 1)

table(sex = sex, pam = fit_pam$cluster)
table(sex = sex, bagged = fit_bag$cluster)
cat("FMI, PAM       :", round(fmi_index(as.integer(sex), fit_pam$cluster), 3), "\n")
cat("FMI, bagged PAM:", round(fmi_index(as.integer(sex), fit_bag$cluster), 3), "\n")
```

## Consensus clustering with a representative shape

`shape_ensemble()` clusters in the leading principal components of the
tangent coordinates (enough components for 90% of the variance, between 2 and
10). It runs k-means on bootstrap samples, builds the co-association matrix of
the replicates and cuts it with a spectral partition. Each cluster also gets a
representative, the observed shape closest to the cluster's Procrustes mean.

```{r ensemble}
fit_ens <- shape_ensemble(sim$X, K = 2, B = 30, seed = 1)
fit_ens
table(truth = sim$group, ensemble = fit_ens$cluster)
```
